title: Baluze 1709: Étienne Baluze (Paris) to the cardinal de Bouillon, 10 May 1709 (Médiathèque Georges-Delaw, Sedan, fonds Gourjault, carton 199, piece 8): cipher transcribed, contemporary decipherment aligned, barred groups found to be nulls, partial key

documents.shelfmark: Médiathèque Georges-Delaw, Sedan, fonds Gourjault, carton 199, piece 8, ff. 24-26

plaintext.source: Contemporary interlinear decipherment, word by word, over every cipher passage except '66 + 95', 'J+' and the end of l. 8.

transcription.source: photographs sent by the Médiathèque Georges-Delaw (not published)
transcription.notes: doubtful shapes settled by a blind reading sheet answered by Brice Dudout (18 Nov 2026, two controls passed); tokens include barred groups and person signs

system.summary: Two-digit groups for letters and syllables with homophones, barred groups as nulls, and a small nomenclator of signs for persons (ɸ, +, J in combination)

diacritics.note: a bar over a group makes it a null (the decipherer writes nothing over it); possible exception 35 in 'vont'

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherment on the letter (carton 199, piece 8), word by word. Nothing on Gourjault, Baluze, Bréant, Réveillon or Sedan in catalogue.json or research/leads.json (main 42068aa8, 19 Nov 2026), in targets/ or in the open pull requests (the only Baluze hits are BnF fonds Baluze shelfmarks of other targets); no printed edition of the decipherment found by web search (18 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the photographs, chose the target and answered a blind reading sheet on doubtful shapes (two controls passed). AI agents transcribed, aligned the decipherment, inferred the partial key and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Cipher of ff. 24-25 transcribed from the library's photographs (about 100 groups and signs); blind reading sheet: 67 (not 65) in 'perd', 57 and 46 confirmed, the 0 of '0 ɸ' a separate digit, the sign after + in '+J' not identified.

Barred groups are nulls: the decipherer writes nothing over them and puts dashes in his clear at their places; with them removed, the words of the decipherment fit the groups (perd = 66 67, si viste = 82 92 86, franchement = 17 75 35 06 36 51). One possible exception (35 in 'vont').

Partial key inferred from the decipherment: 5 values sure (16 de, 34 n, 56 ne, 75 ra, 76 re), 31 probable from one word, 4 conflicts (95, 91, 57, 36); 4 person signs fixed by the gloss (Bignon, the chancellor, Bouillon, Baluze), J+ and '66 + 95' unglossed. The conflicts cannot be settled from one letter.
catalogue.json, research/leads.json, targets and open pull requests searched for Gourjault, Baluze, Bréant, Réveillon, Sedan: nothing; web search: no edition of the decipherment.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The partial key is inferred from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the same letter, kept in two layers: what the decipherment fixes (which groups make which word; the person signs) and what is inferred (group values: 5 sure, 31 probable, 4 in conflict). The content is the decipherment's (existing); no reading of ours is claimed and none is counted.

credits.note: the interlinear decipherment of the time over the cipher passages; the partial key was inferred from it

texts.label: Baluze to the cardinal de Bouillon, Paris, 10 May 1709
texts.summary: Baluze has shown the cardinal's letter to the abbé Bignon, who will serve him with the chancellor; but things do not go so fast, and the chancellor must be brought back from his prejudices.
texts.note: decryption.txt is the contemporary decipherment set against the groups, not a decryption by this project: the key is partial. The summary is from the decipherment.
